title: Sexual size dimorphism in the atyid shrimp Paratya compressa (De Haan, 1844) (Decapoda: Caridea: Atyidae)
content:
Abstract
Sexual size dimorphism in decapod crustaceans is often associated with mating systems shaped by sexual selection. In caridean shrimps, species exhibiting a pure-searching mating system typically have smaller males and reduced weapon development, reflecting selection for mobility rather than combat. In addition to overall body size, other body parts may be morphologically adapted to enhance locomotor performance and reduce predation risk during mate searching. We examined sexual size dimorphism in multiple body parts of the atyid shrimp Paratya compressa (De Haan, 1844) to evaluate whether morphological patterns are consistent with this mating system. Specimens were collected from a river population in Japan, and 11 body dimensions were measured and analyzed using allometric approaches. Males were significantly smaller than females in carapace length (P < 0.0001). Allometric analyses revealed that several body parts differed in relative size between the sexes despite similar growth slopes. Males exhibited relatively larger rostrum, scaphocerite, pleopodal exopod, telson, and uropod. These male-biased traits, associated with locomotor performance and stability, may facilitate mate searching and predator avoidance. Comparison with the congeneric P. improvisa Kemp, 1917 suggests that habitat conditions may influence the expression of sexual size dimorphism. These findings provide new insights into morphological variation associated with mating systems in atyid shrimps.
